bio: Hi! I'm Rafaela Solís, a passionate game designer dedicated to creating engaging, immersive, and emotional player-focused gaming experiences. My journey in game development started as a tiny baby. My father started a company during the tech boom, and performed IT services for the city of Austin, Texas. He always had every kind of computer, and quite often we would sit down together in front of a 4 inch thick laptop to play obscure cobbled together kids games that my tiny brain could understand. I've been hooked ever since.

I double major in Game Design and Game Programming at Champlain College (2028), with a minor in Project Management and specific focus in system design, level design, technical design, narrative design, gameplay programming, rapid prototyping, and more. I have experience with Unreal Engine 5, Unity 6, C++, Lua, C#, Python, Java, Blueprints, and web tools like Astro and Next.js. I love the puzzle of making people happy. I've worked across a plethora of genres and projects: Maze-Puzzle, Action-Adventure, Educational, Drawing-Combat, Multiplayer Coop/Competitive, Website Portfolios, Web Tools, and more!

I've shipped three non-academic large-team project demos: Mega Market Mayhem, Scriptorium, and Open Shift, with Scriptorium and Open Shift in active development. Beyond that, dozens of indie and jam games, and a plethora of academic prototypes and web centered projects, like the one you're on right now! Each project has taught me invaluable lessons about teamwork, scope, design, and the importance of the user.
about.lookingFor: I'm currently seeking passionately led projects and game industry internships in the US, Canada, and EU regions. I'm particularly excited about work involving user psychology, narrative-driven experiences, large-scale multiplayer stacks, and community-driven development.

design.title: Game Designer
design.summary: Game designer pursuing dual B.S. degrees in Game Design and Game Programming with a Project Management minor. Leads design across three studio titles at Pentad Games, prototyping features directly in Unity and Unreal Engine 5 with C++, Lua, and C#, and directing the team that builds them. Placed 2nd internationally in the CurseForge Subnautica 2 Modding Contest, with 6,500+ mod downloads on CurseForge. Programming makes it possible to prototype designs firsthand and work fluently with engineers; production training means leading a team or supporting one.

programming.title: Gameplay Programmer
programming.summary: Gameplay programmer pursuing dual B.S. degrees in Game Programming and Game Design with a Project Management minor. Writes C++ and Lua in Unreal Engine 5 and C# in Unity; placed 2nd internationally in the CurseForge Subnautica 2 Modding Contest, with 6,000+ downloads across Subnautica 2 mods. Lead programmer at Pentad Games, building gameplay systems, CI pipelines, and team tooling. Design training means building systems that serve the player; production training means shipping them on schedule.

production.title: Game Producer
production.summary: Game producer pursuing a Project Management minor alongside dual B.S. degrees in Game Design and Game Programming. Has run weekly Agile/Scrum sprints for 5+ game teams and serves as product owner at Pentad Games, building the studio’s production toolchain from scratch. Hands-on C++, Lua, and C# experience in Unreal Engine 5 and Unity, including a 2nd-place international finish in the CurseForge Subnautica 2 Modding Contest, makes it possible to plan with every discipline in its own language.
